body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvaprātimokṣasūtra</s> (The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva's Code of Liberation)

body.text: om namaḥ sarvvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ / ye ca te bodhisattvānāṃ trayaḥ śīlaskandhā uktāḥ / saṃvara śīlaṃ kuśaladharmmasaṃgrāhakaśīlaṃ sattvārthakriyāśīlaṃ ca teṣu śikṣitukāmena gṛhiṇā vā pravrajitena vā 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtapraṇidhānena sahadhārmmikasya bodhisattvasya mahāpuṇyanidhānasya vāg vijñaptyartha grahaṇāvabodhasamarthasya pādayornnipatyādhyeṣaṇā kāryā / tavāhaṃ kulaputrāyuṣman bhadanteti vā 'ntikāt bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānamākāṅkṣābhyādātum / tadarhasyanuparodhena muhūrttamadanukampayā dātuṃ śrotuñceti // trirevamadhyeṣya ekāṃsamuttarāṅgaṃ kṛtvādaśasu dikṣvatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ sāmīcīṃ kṛttvā teṣāṃ guṇānāmukhīkṛtya ghanarasaṃ cetaḥprasādaṃ saṃjanayya nīcairjānumaṇḍalenotkuṭukena vā sthitvā tathāgatapratimāṃ purataḥ saṃsthāpya saṃpūjya puraskṛtyaivaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! The three aggregates of moral discipline (<s>śīlaskandha</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have been stated: the <s>saṃvaraśīla</s> (restraining discipline), the <s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīla</s> (discipline of gathering wholesome qualities), and the <s>sattvārthakriyāśīla</s> (discipline of working for the benefit of beings). One who wishes to train in these — whether a householder or a renunciant — having made the resolution for unsurpassed perfect awakening, should prostrate at the feet of a fellow <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the <s>Dharma</s>, a great treasury of merit, who is capable of verbal instruction and understanding of meaning, and make this request: "I wish, O son of good family — or Venerable — or Elder — to receive from you the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline." "May you be pleased to grant it with compassion, patiently, for a moment, and to listen." Having made this request three times in this manner, placing the upper robe over one shoulder, having made a respectful bow to the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten directions — past, future, and present — and to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), having contemplated their virtues and generated a deep and concentrated clarity of mind, one should then stand kneeling on both knees or squatting, and having placed a <s>Tathāgata</s> image before oneself, having worshipped and honored it, one should be addressed thus:

body.text: anuprayaccha me kulaputrāyuṣmān bhadanteti vā bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānamiti /
body.translated_text: "Grant me, O son of good family — or Venerable — or Elder — the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline."

body.text: tat ekāgrāṃ smṛtimupasthāpya citta prasādamevānuvṛṃhayata / na cirasyedānī me 'kṣayasyāprameyasya niruttarasya mahāpuṇyanidhānasya prāptirbhaviṣyatīti / evamevārthamanuvicintayatā tūṣṇīṃ bhavitavyam / tena punarvvijñena bodhisattvena sa tathā pratipanno bodhisattvo 'vikṣiptena cetasā sthitena vā niṣaṇṇena vā evaṃ syādvacanīyaḥ / śṛṇu tvamevannāman kulaputrāyuṣman bhadanteti vā bodhisattvo 'si bodhau ca kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ / tena omiti pratijñātavyaṃ / sa punaruttari evaṃsyādvacanīyaḥ / pratīcchasi tvamevannāman kulaputrāyuṣmān bhadanteti vā bodhisattvo 'si bodhau kṛtapraṇidhāno mamāntikāt sarvvāṇi bodhisattvaśikṣāpadāni sarvvañca bodhisattvaśīlaṃ saṃvaraśīlaṃ kuśaladharmmasaṃgrāhakaśīlaṃ sattvārthakriyāśīlaṃ ca yacchīlamatītānāṃ bodhisattvanāmabhūt yāni ca śikṣāpadāni / yacchīlamanāgatānām bodhisattvānāṃ bhaviṣyati yāni ca śikṣāpadāni / yacchīlametarhi daśasu dikṣu pratyutpannānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bhavati yāni ca śikṣāpadāni / yeṣu ca śikṣāpadeṣu yeṣu śīleṣvatītāḥ sarvvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣitavantaḥ / anāgatāḥ sarvvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣiṣyante / pratyutpannāḥ sarvvabodhisattvāḥ śikṣante / tena pratigṛṇhāmīti pratijñātavyaṃ // trirevam //
body.translated_text: Then, establishing one-pointed mindfulness, one should cultivate mental clarity, (thinking): "It will not be long before I obtain the attainment of this inexhaustible, immeasurable, unsurpassed, great treasury of merit." Reflecting thus on this meaning, one should remain silent. Then that wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> should address the one who has so presented himself — that <s>Bodhisattva</s> standing or sitting with an undistracted mind — thus: "Listen, O one named such-and-such, son of good family — or Venerable — or Elder — you are a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has made the resolution for awakening." To this, one should affirm: "Yes." He should then be addressed further: "Do you, O one named such-and-such, son of good family — or Venerable — or Elder — a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has made the resolution for awakening, accept from me all the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training precepts and the entire <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline — the <s>saṃvaraśīla</s> (restraining discipline), the <s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīla</s> (discipline of gathering wholesome qualities), and the <s>sattvārthakriyāśīla</s> (discipline of working for the benefit of beings) — the discipline and training precepts that belonged to past <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the discipline and training precepts that will belong to future <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the discipline and training precepts that belong now to present <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the ten directions — the training precepts and disciplines in which all past <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have trained, all future <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will train, and all present <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are training?" To this, one should affirm: "I accept." This (is done) three times.

body.text: samanvāharantu māṃ daśadiglokadhānusannipatitā buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvāḥ / samanvāharatvācāryyo 'hamevannāmā yatkiñcitkāyavāṅmanobhirbuddha bodhisattvān mātāpitarau tadanyān vā sattvān samāgamyehajanmanyanyeṣu vā janmāṃ tareṣu mayāpāyaṃ kṛtaṃ kāritamanumoditam vā tat sarvvamaikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya piṇḍayitvā tulayitvā sarvvabuddhabodhisattvānāmācāryyasya cāntike 'grayā pravarayā pratideśanayā pratideśayāmi jānan smaran na praticchādayāmi // trirevam //
body.translated_text: "May the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> assembled from the world-realms of the ten directions attend to me! May the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) attend! I, named such-and-such, whatever unwholesome actions I have committed — by body, speech, or mind — in relation to <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, my mother and father, or any other beings, whether in this birth or in other births, whether done by myself, caused to be done by others, or approved — all of that I gather together into one mass, weigh it, and in the presence of all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the <s>ācārya</s>, I confess it with the foremost and supreme confession — knowing, remembering, not concealing." This (is done) three times.

body.text: sohamevaṃnāmā evaṃdeśitātyaya imaṃ divasamupādāya āvodhimaṇḍaniṣadanāt buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahākārūṇikaṃ sarvvajñaṃ sarvvadarśinaṃ sarvvavairabhayātītaṃ mahāpuruṣamabhedyakāyamanuttarakāyaṃ dharmmakāyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam // so 'hamevaṃnāmā evaṃdeśitātyaya imaṃ divasamupādāya ābodhimaṇḍadiṣadanāddharma śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi śāntaṃ virāgāṇāṃ pravaram / so 'hamevaṃnāmā evaṃdeśitātyaya imaṃ divasamupādāya ābodhimaṇḍaniṣadanādavaivarttikabodhisattvasaṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇāṇāṃ śreṣṭham // trirevam //
body.translated_text: "I, named such-and-such, having confessed my transgressions thus, from this day forth until sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), take refuge in the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, the Great Compassionate One, the Omniscient, the All-Seeing, who has transcended all enmity and fear, the Great Being, whose body is indestructible, whose body is unsurpassed, the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), the foremost among bipeds." "I, named such-and-such, having confessed my transgressions thus, from this day forth until sitting at the seat of awakening, take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, the peaceful, the supreme among those free from passion." "I, named such-and-such, having confessed my transgressions thus, from this day forth until sitting at the seat of awakening, take refuge in the <s>Saṅgha</s> of non-retrogressing <s>Bodhisattvas</s> (<s>avaivarttikabodhisattva</s>), the best of assemblies." This (is done) three times.

body.text: sohamevaṃnāmā evaṃdeśitātyayastriśaraṇagato 'nantasattvadhātūttāraṇāyābhyuddharaṇāya saṃsāraduḥkhāt paritrāṇāya sarvvajñajñāne anuttare pratiṣṭhāpanāya / yathā te atītānāgatapratyutpannā bodhisattvā bodhicittamutpādya buddhatvamadhigatavanto 'dhigamiṣyanti adhigacchanti ca / yathā sarvvabuddhā 'nāvaraṇena buddhajñānena buddh cakṣuṣā jānanti paśyanti yathā dharmmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāvatāma(?) nujānanti / tena vidhinā ahamevaṃnāmā evaṃnāmna ācāryyasyāntikāt sarvvabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ ca purato 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpādayāmi // trirevam //
body.translated_text: "I, named such-and-such, having confessed my transgressions and taken the triple refuge, for the purpose of rescuing and liberating the infinite realm of beings, for protecting them from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, for establishing them in the unsurpassed omniscient knowledge — just as those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the past, future, and present, having generated <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), have attained, will attain, and are attaining <s>Buddhahood</s>; just as all <s>Buddhas</s>, with unobstructed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge and <s>Buddha</s>-eye, know and see, just as they understand the essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> — in that same manner, I, named such-and-such, in the presence of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) named such-and-such and before all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, generate the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)." This (is done) three times.

body.text: idaṃ cāhamatyayadeśanātriśaraṇagamanabodhicittotpādajanitaṃ kuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayāmi yadahaṃ loke aśaraṇe alayane aparāyaṇe 'dvipe trāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ layaṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ dvīpo bhaveyam / sarvvasattvāṃśca bhavārṇavādutīrṇastārayeyam / aparinirvṛtānanāvaraṇena dharmmadhātuparinirvāṇena parinirvvāpayeyam / anāśvastānāśvāśayeyam // trirapi //
body.translated_text: "And I dedicate this root of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), born from the confession of transgressions, the taking of the triple refuge, and the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, toward unsurpassed perfect awakening — that I may become a protector, a refuge, a shelter, a resort, and an island for the world that is without refuge, without shelter, without resort, and without island. And, having crossed the ocean of existence (<s>bhavārṇava</s>), may I ferry across all beings. May I bring to final <s>nirvāṇa</s> those who have not yet attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>, through the unobstructed <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth). May I comfort those who are without comfort." This also (is done) three times.

body.text: sohamevaṃnāmā evamutpāditabodhicitto 'nantasattvadhātuṃ yathā mātāpitṛbhaginībhrātṛputraduhitranyatamānyatamajñātisālohitasthānīyāṃstathā pratigṛṇhāmi / pratigṛhya ca yathāśakti yathābalam yathājñānaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ samāropayāmi / itaḥ prabhṛti yatkiñcit dānaṃ dāsyāmi śīlaṃ rakṣiṣyāmi kṣāṃti saṃpādayiṣyāmi vīryamārabhya dhyānaṃ samāpatsye prajñayā vyavacāryya upāyakauśalyaṃ vā śikṣiṣye tat sarvvasattvānāmarthāya hitāya sukhāya //
body.translated_text: "I, named such-and-such, having thus generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, accept the infinite realm of beings as though they were my mother, father, sister, brother, son, daughter, or any other relative and kinsman. Having accepted them, I shall cultivate roots of merit according to my ability, according to my strength, according to my knowledge. From this time forth, whatever generosity (<s>dāna</s>) I shall give, whatever morality (<s>śīla</s>) I shall guard, whatever patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) I shall cultivate, undertaking vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), whatever meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) I shall accomplish, having applied wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), whatever skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) I shall train in — all that shall be for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all beings."

body.text: uttarāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhimārabhya teṣāṃ mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahākāruṇikāṇāṃ mahāyāne sāmicīmanupravrajāmi / anupravrajya bodhisattvo 'haṃ bodhisattva iti māmitaḥ prabhṛtyācāryyo dhārayatu // trirevam //
body.translated_text: "And, undertaking the supreme perfect awakening, I enter the respectful following of those compassionate <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages (<s>mahābhūmi</s>), in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). Having thus entered, may the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) henceforth regard me as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, (saying) 'He is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.'" This (is done) three times.

body.text: tatastenācāryyeṇa tasyāḥ pratimāyāḥ purato daśasu dikṣu buddhabodhisattvānāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyatāṃ yāpayatāṃ pādayornnipatya sāmicīṃ kṛtvā evamārocayitavyam / gṛhītamanenaivaṃnāmnā bodhisattvena mamaivaṃnāmno bodhisattvasyāntikāt yāvat trirapi bodhisatvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānam / sohamevaṃnāmā bodhisattva ātmānaṃ sākṣibhūtaṃ prajānan asyaivaṃnāmno bodhisattvasya paramāryyāṇāṃ viparokṣāṇāmapi sarvatra sarvvasattvānāṃ viparokṣabuddhīnāṃ daśadikṣvanantāparyyanteṣu lokadhātuṣvārocayāmi / asmin bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādānam // trirevam //
body.translated_text: Then that <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), before that image, falling at the feet of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling, abiding, and living in the ten directions, having made a respectful salutation, should announce thus: "This one named such-and-such, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, has received from me, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named such-and-such, the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline (<s>bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvara</s>) — up to three times. I, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named such-and-such, acknowledging myself as witness, announce this to the noble ones (<s>paramārya</s>) beyond sight, and to all beings in the infinite and boundless world-realms (<s>lokadhātu</s>) of the ten directions, whose awareness is beyond our perception — that the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline has been made." This (is done) three times.

body.text: evaṃ punaḥ śīlasaṃvarasamādānakarmmasamāptyanantaraṃ dharmmatā khalveṣā yad daśasu dikṣvanantāparyyantesu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatānāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyatāṃ yāpayatāṃ mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ tadrupaṃ nimittam prādurbhavati yena teṣāmevaṃ bhavati / evaṃnāmnā bodhisattvena evaṃnāmno bodhisattvasyāntikāt bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvara samādānaṃ samāttamiti // evaṃ tāvat parataḥ samādānavidhiruktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, immediately after the completion of the ceremony of undertaking the moral discipline (<s>śīlasaṃvarasamādāna</s>), it is indeed a natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that in the infinite and boundless world-realms (<s>lokadhātus</s>) of the ten directions, a sign manifests to the <s>Tathāgatas</s> who abide, endure, and continue, and to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), by which they know thus: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> named such-and-such has received the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named such-and-such.' Thus, the procedure for receiving (the precepts) from another has been stated.

body.text: yadi tairguṇairyuktaḥ pudgalo na sannihitaḥ syāt tato bodhisattvena tathāgatapratimāyāḥ purataḥ svayamapi bodhisattvaśīlasaṃvarasamādāne vacanīyam / evaṃ ca karaṇīyam / ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā daśasu dikṣvatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ sāmīcīṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya utkuṭukena vā idam syādvacanīyam / ahamevaṃnāmā daśasu dikṣu sarvatathāgatān mahābhūmipraviṣṭāṃśca bodhisattvān vijñāpayāmi / teṣāṃ purataḥ sarvvāṇi bodhisatvaśikṣāpadāni sarvvaṃ ca bodhisattvaśīlaṃ samādade / yacchīlamityādi pūrvvavat yāvat bodhisattvo bodhisattva iti / māmitaḥ prabhṛti buddha bhagavanto bodhisattvāśca dhārayantviti vijñaptiḥ // 0 //
body.translated_text: If a person endowed with those qualities is not available, then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should recite the undertaking of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline by himself before a <s>Tathāgata</s> image. And it should be done thus: having placed the upper robe over one shoulder, having made a respectful bow to the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten directions — past, future, and present — and to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), having placed the right knee on the ground, or squatting, one should say this: 'I, named such-and-such, inform all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the great stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) in the ten directions. In their presence, I accept all the <s>Bodhisattva</s> training precepts and the entire <s>Bodhisattva</s> moral discipline.' The discipline and so forth as before, up to '<s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' The declaration (<s>vijñapti</s>) is: 'May the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> henceforth hold me (as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>).'
